hero.headline: South Korean Stock Trading Halted as Chip Stocks Plunge Across Asia
hero.body:
South Korea's benchmark stock index experienced a sharp decline on Tuesday, forcing temporary trading halts as investors sold off semiconductor stocks amid concerns about artificial intelligence spending and Chinese competition.

The Kospi index fell more than 10 percent by the end of trading, representing one of the steepest single-day drops in recent months. The decline triggered circuit breakers that temporarily paused trading after the index had slumped 8 percent, a mechanism designed to prevent panic selling during severe market movements.

Semiconductor companies including Samsung and SK Hynix saw their shares drop by more than 10 percent as the selloff intensified. The losses extended well beyond South Korea, with chip stocks sliding across Asia and affecting American technology markets. Nasdaq futures slipped following the deepening selloff in Asia, suggesting continued pressure on US technology stocks.

Investors have become increasingly worried about whether artificial intelligence companies can justify the enormous amounts they are spending to expand data center infrastructure. Many AI companies have relied on significant borrowing to fund these expansions, raising questions about the sustainability of such spending levels. Additionally, concerns about potential competition from Chinese semiconductor manufacturers have added to market anxiety.

The semiconductor industry has seen massive capital investments focused on AI-related technology over the past year. However, investors are now questioning whether the financial returns will match these large outlays. Worries about circular funding patterns within the chip sector have contributed to the broader unease affecting markets.

The market turmoil extended beyond technology stocks. Oil prices also retreated as broader market concerns spread across different sectors. This volatility occurred during what analysts described as a critical period for global stock markets.

South Korea's position as one of the world's most important semiconductor manufacturing hubs made the country particularly vulnerable to shifts in investor sentiment about AI spending. South Korean chipmakers have significant exposure to the technology supply chain, meaning they face substantial risk when confidence in AI spending wavers.

The sharp moves in Asian markets have put investors on alert about potential continued pressure on technology stocks globally. The severity of selling pressure in South Korea's market underscored how deeply concerns about AI spending sustainability and Chinese competition are affecting investor confidence in the semiconductor sector.

The temporary trading halt illustrated the intensity of the selloff and highlighted how quickly market sentiment can shift when major investors reassess their positions in technology stocks. As markets continue to process these developments, analysts are monitoring whether the decline will stabilize or if additional losses may follow in coming trading sessions.

cards.headline: Trump pauses Iran bombing campaign around strategic strait
cards.teaser: President Trump ordered U.S. forces to halt bombing operations around the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such pause in the campaign.
cards.body:
President Trump ordered American forces to halt bombing Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's southern coast, marking the first pause in the U.S. air campaign in the region. The pause suggests constraints on what air strikes alone can achieve militarily.

Oil markets responded positively to the pause. Brent crude fell 9% to below $88 a barrel, as traders wagered that reduced U.S. attacks could prevent further conflict escalation that might tighten global energy supplies. The decision reflects sensitivity around the strategically critical waterway, through which substantial portions of world oil supplies transit.

cards.headline: Trump says U.S. in talks with Iran but signals return to military pressure remains possible
cards.teaser: President Trump indicated negotiations are underway with Tehran while warning military action could resume if diplomacy fails.
cards.body:
The U.S. and Iran have paused fighting and exchanged diplomatic messages following nearly two weeks of intense conflict. President Trump has signaled that strong military action could resume if negotiations fail.

Iran's leadership has shown little urgency to return to talks, betting they can withstand prolonged pressure while leveraging control of the Strait of Hormuz. The pause in strikes has created space for diplomacy, though both sides appear positioned for potential escalation.

cards.headline: Iran resists resuming cease-fire talks as U.S. pauses strikes
cards.teaser: Iranian leaders are in no rush to return to negotiations with the United States despite a temporary pause in military action.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have both paused military strikes for a second consecutive day as efforts continue to bring the countries back to negotiations on an interim ceasefire. However, the pause has not yet prompted movement toward diplomatic talks.

Oil markets have responded positively to the de-escalation, with Brent crude dropping 9% to below $88 a barrel after climbing to $100 the previous week. Traders are betting that a continuation of the pause could prevent further conflict that would restrict global oil supplies.

cards.headline: Trump to meet Ukrainian and Israeli leaders
cards.teaser: President Trump scheduled meetings with President Zelenskyy of Ukraine and Prime Minister Netanyahu of Israel.
cards.body:
President Trump will meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday, bringing two key U.S. allies to the White House for back-to-back foreign policy discussions.

During his meeting with Zelenskyy, Ukraine's leader plans to seek stronger U.S. commitments to bolster Kyiv's air defense systems as Russia escalates missile attacks. Netanyahu's visit marks his first encounter with Trump since the Iran conflict began, as both leaders face domestic political pressures.

cards.headline: Zelensky to push Trump for air defense commitments in Washington
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president seeks to secure U.S. pledges to strengthen anti-ballistic missile defenses as Russia intensifies attacks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is seeking to strengthen U.S. commitments to air defense during his Washington meetings with President Trump. Russia's escalating attacks on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure have made bolstering Kyiv's defenses increasingly urgent.

Zelensky aims to secure additional anti-ballistic missile systems from the United States to counter the intensifying Russian strikes targeting civilian areas and critical infrastructure across Ukraine.

cards.headline: Trump immigration program on track for 200,000 departures
cards.teaser: The administration's paid self-deportation program has helped about 132,000 unauthorized immigrants leave the U.S. so far.
cards.body:
President Trump's self-deportation program, which pays unauthorized immigrants to leave the United States, is projected to account for more than 200,000 departures based on internal government data. Through mid-July, the program called Project Homecoming has assisted approximately 132,000 people in leaving the country.

The Department of Homeland Security initiative carries a budget of nearly $600 million and was launched alongside a multimillion-dollar advertising campaign. The program represents one of the few incentive-based components of the administration's immigration enforcement strategy, which has otherwise focused on detention and removal operations.

hero.headline: Magnitude 7.1 earthquake strikes southwestern Japan, people trapped in shopping center
hero.body:
A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the southwestern prefecture of Kumamoto, Japan, trapping people inside a shopping center and causing fires and injuries across the region. Japan's state broadcaster reported that some people remained trapped inside the Aeon Mall in Kumamoto, with some reports indicating an explosion occurred at the shopping center following the quake.

Authorities issued a tsunami warning immediately after the earthquake, though it was later lifted. Fires broke out in multiple locations across Kumamoto prefecture, and injuries were reported, though specific casualty numbers have not been confirmed. Emergency response teams were dispatched to affected areas.

The earthquake struck a region that has experienced significant seismic activity in the past. Kumamoto prefecture, located on the island of Kyushu, sits in one of Japan's most earthquake-prone zones. The magnitude 7.1 quake represents a major seismic event capable of causing widespread structural damage and triggering secondary disasters like fires and building collapses.

Japan maintains one of the world's most advanced earthquake early warning and response systems, designed to alert residents seconds before shaking begins and coordinate rapid emergency response. The country's building codes require structures to withstand significant seismic activity, though older buildings and infrastructure remain vulnerable to major quakes.

Rescue operations were underway at the Aeon Mall and other affected sites across Kumamoto. The full extent of casualties and structural damage was still being assessed as emergency crews worked to reach trapped individuals and extinguish fires. Japanese authorities typically conduct thorough building inspections following major earthquakes to identify structures unsafe for occupancy and coordinate evacuation and relief efforts for affected residents.

cards.headline: Clashes break out in Pakistani Kashmir as regional election begins
cards.teaser: Violence erupted on the first day of a weekslong regional election in Pakistani Kashmir, adding to weeks of deadly unrest.
cards.body:
Violent clashes erupted in Pakistani Kashmir on the first day of a contested regional election. Officials confirmed that dozens of people have died in the weeks leading up to the vote, which is expected to span several weeks.

A banned civil rights group reported that its supporters were killed during confrontations with police. The violence underscores deep tensions in the region, where the election is taking place under tight security measures and restrictions on political activities.

cards.headline: Iran resists resuming cease-fire talks as U.S. pauses strikes
cards.teaser: Iranian leaders are in no rush to return to negotiations with the United States despite a temporary pause in military action.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have both paused military strikes for a second consecutive day as efforts continue to bring the countries back to negotiations on an interim ceasefire. However, the pause has not yet prompted movement toward diplomatic talks.

Oil markets have responded positively to the de-escalation, with Brent crude dropping 9% to below $88 a barrel after climbing to $100 the previous week. Traders are betting that a continuation of the pause could prevent further conflict that would restrict global oil supplies.

cards.headline: Zelensky to push Trump for air defense commitments in Washington
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president seeks to secure U.S. pledges to strengthen anti-ballistic missile defenses as Russia intensifies attacks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is seeking to strengthen U.S. commitments to air defense during his Washington meetings with President Trump. Russia's escalating attacks on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure have made bolstering Kyiv's defenses increasingly urgent.

Zelensky aims to secure additional anti-ballistic missile systems from the United States to counter the intensifying Russian strikes targeting civilian areas and critical infrastructure across Ukraine.

cards.headline: More than 63,000 evacuated near Madrid as wildfires spread across Spain and France
cards.teaser: Tens of thousands fled their homes as wildfires raged across southern Europe, with France issuing heat warnings in affected areas.
cards.body:
Wildfires across Spain and France have forced more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes. At least 63,000 were evacuated near Madrid as blazes spread across both countries. French authorities warned that fires burning near Bordeaux remain far from under control, threatening vineyards in the region.

A new heatwave is expected to complicate firefighting efforts, with temperatures forecast to exceed 40°C in some areas. Spanish Prime Minister warned of "complex hours" ahead as emergency teams race to contain the flames.

cards.headline: U.S. walks out of UN Security Council meeting during France's remarks
cards.teaser: American diplomats left a Security Council session after the U.S. voted against extending the UN human rights chief's term.
cards.body:
The United States walked out of a UN Security Council meeting as France was speaking, triggering diplomatic tensions. The confrontation followed the U.S. vote against extending the term of the UN high commissioner for human rights.

The U.S. position aligned it with North Korea and Russia on the human rights vote—a rare alignment that drew criticism from European allies and strained relations among Western partners on the Security Council.

cards.headline: Trump says U.S. in talks with Iran but signals return to military pressure remains possible
cards.teaser: President Trump indicated negotiations are underway with Tehran while warning military action could resume if diplomacy fails.
cards.body:
The U.S. and Iran have paused fighting and exchanged diplomatic messages following nearly two weeks of intense conflict. President Trump has signaled that strong military action could resume if negotiations fail.

Iran's leadership has shown little urgency to return to talks, betting they can withstand prolonged pressure while leveraging control of the Strait of Hormuz. The pause in strikes has created space for diplomacy, though both sides appear positioned for potential escalation.

hero.headline: New York City property owners notified of pied-à-terre tax
hero.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled two competing budget proposals to address the city's growing fiscal crisis, triggering significant pushback from political leaders across the city and state.

Mamdani's first proposal would raise income and corporate taxes on the city's wealthiest residents and corporations, a move that requires approval from Governor Kathy Hochul. His alternative proposal would increase property taxes by 9.5%, which could affect more than 3 million single-family homes, co-ops, and condos, along with over 100,000 commercial buildings.

"The first path is the most sustainable and fairest: raising taxes on the wealthiest and corporations, and ending the drain by fixing the imbalance between what the City provides the State and what we receive in return," Mamdani said. He warned that rejecting the income tax approach would force the city down "a more harmful path of property taxes and raiding our reserves."

The city faces a budget deficit expected to grow to 7 billion dollars over the next two years, up from 5.4 billion dollars. Hochul has pledged to contribute 1.5 billion dollars in state funding to help close the gap, but has ruled out approving income tax increases.

The property tax increase proposal has drawn swift criticism from city officials across the political spectrum. City Comptroller Mark Levine called it "a pretty extreme option," while City Council Speaker Julie Menin and Finance Committee Chair Linda Lee said raising property taxes during an affordability crisis is inappropriate. Queens Borough President Donovan Richards called a 9.5 percent property tax increase "a nonstarter," saying the city should not "balance our budget on the backs of working-class New Yorkers, especially seniors on fixed incomes."

Republican Council Member David Carr characterized raising property taxes as "among the worst ideas imaginable," describing it as one of the most regressive taxes the city levies.

Governor Hochul told reporters she does not believe a property tax increase is necessary.

Mamdani's budget proposals come as he inherited a larger deficit than expected from his predecessor, Eric Adams. The proposals align with campaign promises to make top earners and corporations contribute more to fund ambitious programs including free childcare, free buses, and rent freezes for one million rent-stabilized apartments.

City Council Speaker Menin acknowledged that budget negotiations typically involve significant back-and-forth between the mayor and city council, but expressed hope for more coordinated discussions going forward. She told media outlets she has been engaging "very constructively" with Mamdani about the budget proposals.

The competing proposals are expected to trigger prolonged negotiations between city and state officials before final budget decisions are made.

cards.headline: US walks out of UN Security Council meeting during French remarks
cards.teaser: The United States left a UN Security Council session while France was speaking, following a vote on the UN human rights chief.
cards.body:
The United States walked out of a UN Security Council meeting during France's remarks, creating a visible rupture between the two longtime allies. The dramatic exit followed a Security Council vote on extending the UN high commissioner for human rights' term.

The US voted against the extension, joining North Korea and Russia in opposition. This alignment with two adversarial nations underscored the depth of the disagreement and the public nature of the dispute at the international body.

cards.headline: England to offer technical subjects to students starting at age 14
cards.teaser: The government plans to introduce technical courses including AI and manufacturing for pupils as young as 14, linked to local job markets.
cards.body:
Schools in England will introduce technical courses for students from age 14, the government has announced. The curriculum will include subjects such as artificial intelligence and manufacturing, designed to connect learning with local employment opportunities.

The initiative aims to provide earlier exposure to career-focused education and align schooling more closely with regional job markets.

cards.headline: Senator Lindsey Graham honored at funeral services in Washington
cards.teaser: World leaders gathered in Washington for funeral services honoring the late Senator Lindsey Graham.
cards.body:
Washington held two days of funeral ceremonies for the late South Carolina Republican senator, beginning Tuesday at the US Capitol. The services drew international attention, with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy among the mourners. Donald Trump delivered a tribute during the Capitol service, and both leaders met with Trump at the White House following the ceremony.

Wednesday's services continued in Graham's home state, featuring an F-16 flyover at the South Carolina state house in Columbia, followed by a public service at First Baptist Church. A private family burial took place in Pickens County, where Graham was born. His younger sister, Darline, succeeded him in the Senate.

cards.headline: Senator Mitch McConnell extends Senate leave, remains hospitalized
cards.teaser: Senator Mitch McConnell will extend his absence from the Senate and has not been medically cleared to return to work.
cards.body:
Senator Mitch McConnell remains hospitalized and has not been cleared to resume his Senate duties, his office confirmed six weeks after he fell at his home in mid-June. The Kentucky Republican is undergoing intense physical therapy as he works to return to his responsibilities.

McConnell's office released a new photograph of the senator alongside the health update. Governor Andy Beshear has called on McConnell to either disclose more details about his condition or resign from office.

cards.headline: Democrats propose anti-corruption reforms as check on Trump
cards.teaser: Democratic lawmakers are advancing ethics reform proposals, arguing the system needs overhauling after past norm violations.
cards.body:
Democrats are pushing anti-corruption reforms, arguing that Trump violated ethics norms during his administration. They contend that now is the time to address these concerns and implement structural changes to government ethics rules.

The party is framing these measures as a necessary check on Trump while responding to voter frustration with a political system they see as working against their interests. Democrats say the reforms are needed to overhaul a system voters believe has been co-opted by special interests.

cards.headline: AI tokens tracked by economists as measure of AI adoption
cards.teaser: Economists are using AI tokens to track how artificial intelligence spreads through the economy.
cards.body:
AI companies use tokens to track usage and bill customers for their services. Economists have now adopted tokens as a metric to measure how artificial intelligence is spreading through the economy.

The comparison mirrors how kilowatt-hours quantify electricity consumption. By monitoring token usage, economists can standardize measurements of AI adoption across different sectors and applications, creating a clearer picture of the technology's economic impact.

cards.headline: Taiwan Detains Nvidia Employee in Chip Smuggling Investigation
cards.teaser: Taiwan authorities detained an Nvidia employee as part of a probe into allegations of smuggling advanced chips to China.
cards.body:
Taiwan prosecutors detained an Nvidia employee in connection with an investigation into Super Micro and allegations of smuggling semiconductor chips to China. The detention was confirmed by a source familiar with the case.

The probe centers on concerns about the export of advanced AI chips that may violate trade restrictions. Taiwan has been working to prevent the illegal transfer of sensitive semiconductor technology to China amid ongoing tensions over chip exports and national security concerns.

cards.headline: UK Prime Minister Proposes Public Control Model for Utilities
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Andy Burnham criticized Margaret Thatcher's privatization policies and outlined an alternative economic model focused on public ownership of utilities.
cards.body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has proposed a different approach to running utilities, arguing against the privatization policies instituted by Margaret Thatcher in the 1980s. Burnham characterized the debate as a choice between public control and what he termed 20th-century socialism.

The prime minister wants to establish an alternative economic model, particularly for essential services like utilities. The proposal represents a significant shift in how the UK government approaches public services and infrastructure management, moving away from decades of private sector control in these industries.

cards.headline: European Police Say Binance Hampers Criminal Investigations
cards.teaser: Law enforcement officials in Europe accused cryptocurrency exchange Binance of making it harder to track scammers and solve crimes.
cards.body:
Investigators in Europe said that Binance, the cryptocurrency giant, has made it more difficult to track down scammers and solve other crimes. The complaints from police officials represent growing friction between law enforcement and the digital currency industry.

The concerns center on how Binance's platform and policies affect the ability of investigators to trace criminal activity and identify perpetrators. Cryptocurrency exchanges have faced increasing scrutiny from regulators and law enforcement over their role in financial crimes and the challenges they pose for traditional investigative methods.

cards.headline: England to Offer Technical Courses to 14-Year-Olds in Education Shift
cards.teaser: The UK government plans to introduce courses in AI and manufacturing linked to local job markets for pupils starting at age 14.
cards.body:
England's schools will begin offering technical courses to 14-year-old pupils, Education Secretary Andy Burnham has announced. The new program will include subjects such as artificial intelligence and manufacturing, with courses designed to connect to job opportunities in local areas.

The initiative marks a significant change in how secondary education is structured in England, introducing vocational and technical training earlier in students' academic paths. By aligning courses with regional employment needs, the government aims to prepare young people for careers in sectors with growing demand.

cards.headline: Private Conversations With Claude AI Found Publicly Accessible Online
cards.teaser: Hundreds of chats with Anthropic's Claude chatbot were discovered to be publicly available on the internet.
cards.body:
Hundreds of conversations with Claude, the chatbot created by Anthropic, were found to be publicly accessible online. The discovery raised concerns about the privacy protections surrounding AI chatbot interactions.

The publicly available conversations were discovered through internet searches, revealing that some users' exchanges with the AI assistant had become searchable and viewable by anyone. Anthropic had not previously disclosed that certain chats with Claude could be made public or indexed by search engines.

cards.headline: School Districts Build Housing to Recruit Teachers Amid National Shortage
cards.teaser: An increasing number of school districts are constructing homes for teachers as the housing shortage makes it hard for educators to afford living where they work.
cards.body:
Facing a national housing shortage that makes it difficult for teachers to afford homes in their communities, school districts across the country are turning to residential construction as a recruitment and retention strategy. The initiative addresses a particular challenge for educators, whose salaries often fail to keep pace with local housing costs.

By investing in housing development, districts aim to attract qualified teachers to areas where they're needed most. This approach signals a shift in how school systems are tackling workforce challenges in an increasingly competitive labor market for educators.

hero.headline: Lyft and Baidu begin robotaxi testing in London
hero.body:
Lyft and Baidu have launched autonomous vehicle testing in London, marking the entry of two major technology companies into the city's emerging robotaxi market. Baidu's Apollo Go self-driving vehicles will be available through Freenow, the European mobility network that Lyft acquired in 2025.

The partnership combines Baidu's autonomous driving technology with Lyft's established ride-hailing infrastructure in Europe. Apollo Go has been operating autonomous taxi services in several Chinese cities, and this expansion represents the company's first deployment in the United Kingdom. Freenow operates across multiple European markets and provides Baidu with an existing customer base and operational framework.

London has become a testing ground for autonomous vehicle companies seeking to demonstrate their technology in dense urban environments. The city's complex traffic patterns, narrow streets, and mix of pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles present technical challenges that differ from the suburban and highway settings where many robotaxi services first launched. Multiple companies are now competing to establish autonomous ride-hailing services in the capital.

The testing phase will allow Baidu to collect data on how its vehicles perform in London conditions and refine the technology before any potential commercial launch. Lyft's acquisition of Freenow in 2025 positioned the company to expand beyond its traditional North American market and compete with other ride-hailing services in Europe. The addition of autonomous vehicles could differentiate Freenow from competitors and reduce long-term operational costs.

Regulatory frameworks for autonomous vehicles in the UK continue to develop as technology companies push forward with testing and deployment plans. The collaboration between Lyft and Baidu demonstrates how established ride-hailing companies are partnering with autonomous vehicle developers rather than building the technology entirely in-house. The outcome of testing in London could influence how quickly robotaxis become available to the general public in the UK and other European cities.

cards.headline: Cursor expands in India ahead of reported SpaceX acquisition
cards.teaser: The coding tool company has launched localized pricing and plans to increase hiring as India becomes its third-largest market.
cards.body:
Cursor has expanded its presence in India with localized pricing, recognizing the country as its third-largest market globally. The company plans to increase local hiring and strengthen its enterprise sales operations in the region.

The expansion coincides with Cursor's reported acquisition by SpaceX, as the coding tool company works to deepen its foothold among Indian developers.

cards.headline: Apple planning redesigned MacBook Ultra
cards.teaser: Apple is working on a new MacBook design as part of a broader overhaul of its computer lineup to support AI features.
cards.body:
Apple is developing a MacBook Ultra with an entirely new design, according to reports on the company's product plans. The redesign is part of a larger effort to update MacBooks and the iMac line to meet increased demands from artificial intelligence applications.

The company is targeting changes across its consumer computer lineup as AI processing requirements push hardware specifications higher. Apple has not announced release dates or specific features for the new MacBook models.

cards.headline: JWST examines stars suspected of hosting Dyson spheres
cards.teaser: The space telescope observed two stars that showed unusual infrared signatures potentially consistent with megastructures.
cards.body:
The James Webb Space Telescope has completed observations of two stars that astronomers identified as candidates for hosting Dyson spheres, hypothetical megastructures that could surround stars to capture their energy. The stars exhibited unusual infrared signatures that prompted the follow-up study.

Dyson spheres remain theoretical constructs proposed as a way advanced civilizations might harness stellar energy. The JWST observations sought to determine whether natural astrophysical phenomena could explain the infrared patterns or whether the signatures warranted further investigation as potential technosignatures.

cards.headline: Hugging Face platform used to create nonconsensual deepfakes
cards.teaser: The AI model repository is hosting tools that enable users to generate fake nude images of women and children.
cards.body:
According to a report by European nonprofit AI Forensics, seven of the nine most popular image editing models hosted on Hugging Face readily generate nonconsensual deepfake images. The open-source AI repository has done little to prevent the misuse of these tools, which are being used to create fake nude images of women and children.

Hugging Face's design as an open platform for sharing machine learning models has enabled the distribution of these harmful tools. The case highlights the tension between supporting legitimate AI research and development while preventing the proliferation of applications designed to create nonconsensual intimate imagery.

cards.headline: Buck Moon rises Wednesday night
cards.teaser: July's full moon will be visible in the night sky on Wednesday.
cards.body:
The full moon in July, known as the Buck Moon, will rise Wednesday night. The name comes from the time of year when male deer grow new antlers.

Full moons occur when the moon is on the opposite side of Earth from the sun, allowing the entire face visible from Earth to be illuminated. The Buck Moon is one of twelve or thirteen full moons that occur each year.

cards.headline: BuzzBallz packaging may not be recyclable as claimed
cards.teaser: The company's website states the plastic containers are recyclable, but experts say this is inaccurate.
cards.body:
BuzzBallz, a brand of premixed cocktails sold in distinctive spherical plastic containers, claims on its website that the packaging is recyclable. However, waste management experts dispute this claim, saying the containers are not actually recyclable.

The disconnect highlights a broader issue in waste management: while some plastic materials can theoretically be recycled, many communities lack the necessary equipment or programs to process them. This means that even technically recyclable materials may not be accepted by local recycling facilities.

hero.headline: Zinedine Zidane named France national team head coach
hero.body:
Zinedine Zidane has been confirmed as the new head coach of the France national football team. The former Real Madrid manager takes charge of the national side, marking his return to management after leaving the Spanish club.

Zidane enjoyed a storied playing career with France, winning the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000. As a manager, he led Real Madrid to three consecutive Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018, establishing himself as one of the most successful coaches in European football. His appointment comes as France looks to build on its strong international record in recent years.

The 54-year-old brings significant experience to the role, having managed at the highest level of club football. During his two spells at Real Madrid, Zidane won 11 trophies including three Champions League titles, two La Liga championships, and two Spanish Super Cups. His tactical acumen and ability to manage star players made him one of the most respected figures in world football.

Zidane inherits a French squad that has remained competitive on the international stage. The team features a blend of experienced players and emerging talent, providing the new coach with strong resources as he takes over. His familiarity with many French players, both from his own era and through his work in Spanish football, is expected to facilitate his transition into the role.

The appointment represents a significant moment for French football. Zidane's status as one of the nation's greatest ever players, combined with his proven success as a manager, has generated considerable anticipation about what he can achieve with the national team. His first matches in charge will be closely watched as he begins to implement his vision for French football on the international stage.

cards.headline: Northampton to open Premiership title defense against Newcastle
cards.teaser: Premiership champions Northampton will host Newcastle on the opening weekend of the 2026-27 rugby season.
cards.body:
Reigning Premiership champions Northampton will host Newcastle in the opening fixture of the 2026-27 season. The match kicks off the new campaign for both clubs.

In the other opening weekend fixture, Exeter will welcome Gloucester to their home ground.

cards.headline: Chelsea target older players after focus on youth
cards.teaser: Chelsea are pursuing deals for Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck as they shift toward signing experienced players.
cards.body:
Chelsea are pursuing transfers for three experienced players: Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson, and Danny Welbeck. The pursuit marks a shift in the club's transfer strategy, moving away from its recent emphasis on younger talent.

The signings would bring veteran experience and leadership to a Chelsea squad that has prioritized youth acquisitions in recent transfer windows.

cards.headline: Chloe Kelly optimistic about Arsenal prospects after difficult season
cards.teaser: Arsenal forward Chloe Kelly says she needed the summer break after finding the 2025-26 season challenging.
cards.body:
Chloe Kelly has described the 2025-26 season as difficult but expressed optimism about the upcoming campaign for both herself and Arsenal. The forward said she needed the summer break to recover from a challenging year.

Kelly is looking forward to the new season with renewed confidence. She believes both her individual prospects and Arsenal's chances have improved heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

cards.headline: Jack Draper withdraws from tournament due to recurring arm injury
cards.teaser: Former British number one Jack Draper has pulled out of another tournament on the eve of competition because of his long-term arm injury.
cards.body:
Jack Draper has withdrawn from a tournament on the eve of the event due to his recurring long-term arm injury. The former British number one has been dealing with the persistent issue throughout his career.

The latest withdrawal continues a pattern of injury-related pullouts affecting Draper's tournament participation.

cards.headline: Rangers face few excuses as McInnes era begins
cards.teaser: Rangers enter the new season with an experienced manager in the dugout, striker Lawrence Shankland leading the attack, and additional financial support.
cards.body:
Rangers are positioned to compete strongly in the upcoming season under their new management structure. The club has an experienced figurehead in the dugout and has brought in Lawrence Shankland to spearhead the attack.

The team also benefits from further financial backing as it prepares for the campaign. With these resources in place, expectations are high for Rangers to perform this season.

cards.headline: Questions mount over Adam Ramsay-Peaty's future after Commonwealth Games
cards.teaser: Former Olympic champion Adam Ramsay-Peaty faces uncertainty about his career prospects after a disappointing Commonwealth Games performance.
cards.body:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty won bronze in the men's 50m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games, a result that has prompted questions about his future in the sport. The British Olympic gold medallist's performance at the Games has sparked debate among observers.

The disappointing showing has left uncertainty over whether the former champion can return to his previous level of success or if he may be approaching the end of his competitive career.

hero.headline: Judge orders singer D4vd to stand trial in killing of 14-year-old
hero.body:
A Los Angeles judge has ruled there is sufficient evidence for singer D4vd to stand trial in the killing of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. The decision came after a four-day preliminary hearing in which prosecutors presented evidence of murder and child sexual abuse charges. D4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, has pleaded not guilty.

During the hearing, prosecutors revealed that Burke had engaged in a sexual relationship with Rivas Hernandez beginning when he was 18 and she was 13. Text messages presented in court showed that Rivas Hernandez became pregnant and later obtained an abortion. In a January 2024 message, Burke apologized for "putting her through this," and Rivas Hernandez responded that neither of them could care for a baby. She was 13 at the time.

The teenager appeared deeply affected by the abortion. In an August 2024 text, she wrote to Burke that she had "killed my kid for you" and expressed sadness about the situation, saying she would do anything to have the baby back. Prosecutors argue Burke fatally stabbed Rivas Hernandez in April 2025 to prevent her from revealing details of their sexual relationship as his music career advanced.

Evidence presented during the hearing included explicit photographs the pair had taken of each other. A detective testified about the images while Rivas Hernandez's parents briefly left the courtroom. The prosecution also showed text messages in which Burke referenced encounters with police and suggested the couple elope to Italy.

In February 2024, Burke told police officers he believed Rivas Hernandez was 18 years old, according to video presented earlier in the week. One message showed Burke writing that he could not wait to move in together without "the cops bitching baby."

The autopsy revealed that Rivas Hernandez died from multiple penetrating injuries. The medical examiner identified two stab wounds, one to her abdomen that struck her liver and another to her left chest that damaged her ribs. The doctor noted that the teenager's remains did not show hesitation marks typically associated with self-inflicted injuries.

Rivas Hernandez's body was discovered last September in the front trunk of a Tesla registered to Burke, approximately five months after prosecutors allege he killed her. The remains were significantly decomposed, making it difficult to determine the exact time of death.

The preliminary hearing serves as a threshold to establish probable cause. The standard of proof required at this stage is lower than the beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standard needed for conviction at trial. Burke will now face a full criminal trial before a jury, who will determine his guilt or innocence. The trial date has not yet been set. If convicted, he could face a significant prison sentence.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande sues hackers who leaked unreleased music and videos
cards.teaser: The pop star has filed legal action seeking to identify hackers who obtained and distributed unreleased songs and photos.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against hackers who obtained and leaked unreleased music, videos, and photographs. The legal action seeks to discover the identities of the individuals responsible for accessing and distributing the private material.

The suit follows a breach that resulted in unreleased tracks and visual content appearing online without authorization. Grande's legal team is pursuing the case to hold those responsible accountable and to prevent further unauthorized distribution of her creative work. The lawsuit represents an effort to protect intellectual property rights in an era of increasing digital security challenges for artists.

cards.headline: Naga Munchetty leaves BBC Breakfast after 17 years
cards.teaser: The longtime BBC One morning show co-host is moving to present Radio 5 Live Breakfast.
cards.body:
Naga Munchetty is leaving BBC Breakfast after 17 years as co-host of the BBC One show. She will move to Radio 5 Live, where she will present Radio 5 Live Breakfast.

The presenter has been a key part of the flagship morning television program since 2009, and her departure marks the end of a lengthy tenure on one of Britain's most-watched breakfast shows.

cards.headline: Translator of The Odyssey pans Christopher Nolan film adaptation
cards.teaser: A scholar who translated Homer's epic writes a critical review, contrasting with praise from film critics.
cards.body:
Emily Wilson, a classicist whose 2017 translation of Homer's Odyssey was cited by Christopher Nolan in early publicity for the film, has strongly criticized the adaptation. Wilson said the film "has nothing convincing to say" and "lacks psychological, emotional, political and ethical depth," describing it as grandiose and superficial.

The negative assessment contrasts sharply with the film's rave reviews from critics and commercial success. Despite Nolan having praised Wilson's translation work in promoting the project, she expressed deep disappointment with his cinematic interpretation of the classic epic poem.

cards.headline: Kaitlan Collins says Trump insults happen regularly in Oval Office
cards.teaser: The CNN chief White House correspondent told Jon Stewart she was unsurprised by the president's remarks at the White House Correspondents Dinner.
cards.body:
CNN chief White House correspondent Kaitlan Collins said she was not surprised when President Donald Trump insulted her during his speech at the White House Correspondents Dinner on Friday. Speaking on The Daily Show with Jon Stewart, Collins indicated such treatment occurs frequently.

Collins told Stewart that the president's behavior at the dinner mirrored what happens regularly during interactions inside the Oval Office. Her comments shed light on the often contentious relationship between the Trump administration and members of the White House press corps, particularly those from CNN, which the president has frequently criticized.

cards.headline: Lee Chang-dong's Possible Love sets theatrical release ahead of Netflix debut
cards.teaser: The film will premiere at Venice and Toronto festivals before opening in theaters worldwide in September and October.
cards.body:
Director Lee Chang-dong's film Possible Love will open in Korean theaters on September 23, followed by select theatrical releases in Australia on October 22 and in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, and Japan on October 23. The film will then stream globally on Netflix starting November 6.

The movie will have its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival and its North American premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival. The staggered release strategy allows for festival exposure and theatrical runs in key markets before the streaming debut, a distribution approach increasingly common for prestige films acquired by streaming platforms.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Discovery acquires Kill Jackie for HBO Max in Europe
cards.teaser: The Catherine Zeta-Jones revenge thriller will stream on HBO Max in Spain, Portugal, and Nordic countries.
cards.body:
Warner Bros. Discovery has acquired the revenge thriller Kill Jackie, starring Catherine Zeta-Jones, for HBO Max in multiple European markets. The deal covers Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, France, and Belgium.

The acquisition includes two of HBO's most established streaming markets, the Nordic countries and Spain, where HBO services launched as early as 2012. The film features Zeta-Jones in a leading role as a character described as glamorous and lethal. The European acquisition represents a significant territorial pickup for the thriller across HBO Max's European footprint.

hero.headline: Trump and Senate leader clash over canceling August recess for voting bill
hero.body:
President Trump and Senate Majority Leader John Thune are at odds over whether the Senate should cancel its August recess to debate voting legislation. The disagreement centers on the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, which Trump has made his top legislative priority.

Thune warned against spending Senate floor time on a bill that has already failed multiple votes. The South Dakota Republican's resistance represents a significant break with the president on legislative strategy and calendar management. Trump has pushed for the Senate to remain in session through August to advance the SAVE America Act, which focuses on voter eligibility requirements.

The dispute highlights tension between the White House and Senate Republican leadership over priorities and tactics. Thune, who leads the Senate majority, controls the chamber's schedule and determines which bills receive floor time. His pushback suggests he views continued debate on the voting bill as unlikely to produce a different result than previous failed votes.

The August recess traditionally gives senators time in their home states. Canceling it would keep lawmakers in Washington during a period typically reserved for constituent meetings and campaign activities. With control of Congress at stake in upcoming elections, the timing adds political weight to the scheduling decision.

The SAVE America Act's repeated failures on the Senate floor indicate it lacks the votes needed to advance, making Thune's calculation about floor time particularly relevant. The majority leader's willingness to publicly oppose the president's top legislative priority signals he is prioritizing what he sees as productive use of Senate time over accommodating White House demands. The standoff leaves unclear whether Trump will continue pressing for the August session or shift focus to other legislative goals.

cards.headline: Trump to meet Ukrainian and Israeli leaders
cards.teaser: President Trump scheduled meetings with President Zelenskyy of Ukraine and Prime Minister Netanyahu of Israel.
cards.body:
President Trump will meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday, bringing two key U.S. allies to the White House for back-to-back foreign policy discussions.

During his meeting with Zelenskyy, Ukraine's leader plans to seek stronger U.S. commitments to bolster Kyiv's air defense systems as Russia escalates missile attacks. Netanyahu's visit marks his first encounter with Trump since the Iran conflict began, as both leaders face domestic political pressures.

cards.headline: Trump pauses Iran bombing campaign around strategic strait
cards.teaser: President Trump ordered U.S. forces to halt bombing operations around the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such pause in the campaign.
cards.body:
President Trump ordered American forces to halt bombing Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's southern coast, marking the first pause in the U.S. air campaign in the region. The pause suggests constraints on what air strikes alone can achieve militarily.

Oil markets responded positively to the pause. Brent crude fell 9% to below $88 a barrel, as traders wagered that reduced U.S. attacks could prevent further conflict escalation that might tighten global energy supplies. The decision reflects sensitivity around the strategically critical waterway, through which substantial portions of world oil supplies transit.

cards.headline: Trump immigration program on track for 200,000 departures
cards.teaser: The administration's paid self-deportation program has helped about 132,000 unauthorized immigrants leave the U.S. so far.
cards.body:
President Trump's self-deportation program, which pays unauthorized immigrants to leave the United States, is projected to account for more than 200,000 departures based on internal government data. Through mid-July, the program called Project Homecoming has assisted approximately 132,000 people in leaving the country.

The Department of Homeland Security initiative carries a budget of nearly $600 million and was launched alongside a multimillion-dollar advertising campaign. The program represents one of the few incentive-based components of the administration's immigration enforcement strategy, which has otherwise focused on detention and removal operations.

cards.headline: Democrats express frustration with party chair Martin
cards.teaser: Democratic National Committee members say they have lost patience with DNC Chair Ken Martin during what some view as a troubled tenure.
cards.body:
Democrats say they have grown impatient with Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin amid ongoing problems during his leadership of the national party. Some party members believe the situation surrounding Martin has become a distraction as Democrats work to win congressional majorities in upcoming elections.

The discontent within the party comes as the DNC faces organizational challenges. Party officials see the leadership situation as pulling focus from electoral priorities at a time when Democrats are trying to flip control of Congress.

cards.headline: Analysis examines Democratic Party's shift toward progressive policies
cards.teaser: An opinion piece argues that Senator Bernie Sanders has reshaped the Democratic Party despite limited legislative achievements.
cards.body:
Senator Bernie Sanders may not have passed significant legislation during 35 years in Congress and two presidential campaigns, but the independent Vermont senator has fundamentally reshaped the Democratic Party, according to a new analysis. Members of the Democratic National Committee's Rules and Bylaws Committee are operating within a party structure influenced by Sanders' political vision.

The assessment suggests that Sanders' impact on the party extends beyond policy wins to broader changes in Democratic priorities and approach. The piece describes Democrats as now functioning within a party that reflects the independent senator's influence on progressive politics and party direction.

cards.headline: FDA recalls thyroid medication nationwide
cards.teaser: Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets were pulled from the market because they are not fully effective, the Food and Drug Administration said.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration announced a nationwide recall of Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets. The agency said the thyroid medication was recalled because it does not work as effectively as required.

Levothyroxine is commonly prescribed to treat hypothyroidism and other thyroid conditions. The FDA did not provide information about which manufacturer produced the recalled tablets or how many units are affected by the recall.
